chunks: From him, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the roof, can one sleep upon it without an enclosure? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade from that'. So I asked him (peace be upon him) about three walls, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless it is four'. I said, 'How much should the height of the walls be?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The shortest of it is one cubit and one open-palms width (Shibr)'.

key_terms.السَّطْحِ: Roof or flat surface of a building
key_terms.ذِرَاعٌ: Cubit, a traditional unit of length
key_terms.شِبْرٌ: Span, the distance from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for walls to sleep on a roof without it being considered exposed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the specific architectural requirements for *satar* (privacy) when sleeping on an open roof, reflecting the Shia emphasis on modesty (*haya*) and the protection of one's private space from public view. It clarifies that while three walls may suffice in some contexts, the preferred and prohibited absence is a full enclosure, with the minimum height of the shortest wall set at one cubit and one *shibr* (approximately 50-60 cm), ensuring adequate visual screening. This ruling underscores the jurisprudential principle that privacy is not merely about physical separation but also about maintaining dignity and preventing accidental exposure.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the roof, can one sleep upon it without an enclosure?’ Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww forbade from that’. So I asked himasws about three walls, so heasws said: ‘No, unless it is four’. I said, ‘How much should the height of the walls be?’ Heasws said: ‘The shortest of it is one cubit and one open-palms width (Shibr)’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about sleeping overnight on a flat roof without fencing wall around it. He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited it.’ I then asked if three yards (Zira’ arm-length) is sufficient for the height of such fencing wall. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is four.’ I then asked, ‘How much is the length of the wall?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The shortest is one yard (Zira’ arm-length) and one Shibr. (the distance from the tip of the thump to the tip of the little finger with the thump and little finger open and stretched out).”’
